title: 3D insights into SN 1987A: ALMA observations compared to hydrodynamical explosion simulations
question: How do the three-dimensional spatial and velocity distributions of CO and SiO molecules in the ejecta of SN 1987A observed with ALMA compare with long-time 3D hydrodynamical supernova explosion simulations across different progenitor models, and what do they imply for the neutron-star kick direction?

data.bands: Band 7 (for dust continuum); others not stated by band number
data.angular_resolution: 0.03–0.06 arcsec (up to ~0.11 arcsec for epoch 2 SiO 6-5 and CO 6-5)
data.sensitivity: 0.04 mJy/beam (CO 2-1 ep1), 2.82 mJy/beam (CO 6-5 ep1), 0.05 mJy/beam (SiO 5-4 ep1), 0.033 mJy/beam (SiO 5-4 ep2), 0.06 mJy/beam (SiO 6-5 ep1), 0.055 mJy/beam (SiO 6-5 ep2)

evidence.quote: To convert angular distances to physical distances in the $x$-$y$ plane, we adopt the distance to SN 1987A of 51.4 kpc found by (cite: Panagia.1999)

what.value: Systemic heliocentric velocity of SN 1987A / LMC of +287 +/- 3 km s^-1

evidence.quote: In the $z$-direction, we first subtracted the systemic velocity of the LMC, $v_{\rm hel}$=+287$\pm$3 km s$^{-1}$ (cite: Meaburn.1995; Groningsson:2008jb) from the observed velocity values.

what.value: Geometric centre of the equatorial ring as explosion origin: alpha=05:35:27.9875(11), delta=-69:16:11.107(4) (ICRF J2015.0)

evidence.quote: We use the position determined by (cite: Alp.2018), who calculated the geometric centre of the equatorial ring by fitting an ellipse to the locations of the centroids of its bright clumps.

what.value: Inclination of the equatorial ring (~43 deg to the plane of the sky)

evidence.quote: The equatorial ring appears elliptical as it is inclined at $\sim$43$^\circ$ to the plane of the sky ((cite: 2011A&A...527A..35T)).

what.value: 3D map of [Fe I] emission in the ejecta of SN 1987A

evidence.loc: Comparison of SiO and CO morphologies
evidence.quote: Interestingly, (cite: 2023ApJ...949L..27L) find that \[Fe i\] emission in the ejecta resembles a broken dipole, with two large clumps at velocities of approximately 2300 km s$^{-1}$.

recipe.goal: Grid the ejecta region, determine noise threshold, and extract integrated line profiles
recipe.method: Select a 0.6" x 0.6" region covering the ejecta (excluding the equatorial ring) and divide it into a 10x10 grid of 0.06" x 0.06" cells. Estimate the noise threshold by taking four regions outside the equatorial ring, dividing each into 10x10 cells, computing the mean absolute deviation (MAD) in each cell, and taking the mean of all MAD values. Mask out data below this threshold and integrate the spectrum over all spatial cells.
key_parameters: 0.6" x 0.6" region, 10x10 grid (0.06" x 0.06" per cell), velocity binning 100 or 300 km s^-1
assumptions: Four off-source regions outside the equatorial ring contain no signal from circumstellar material

recipe.goal: Construct 3D spatial maps of CO and SiO emission and measure hemispheric asymmetries
recipe.method: Convert sky pixel coordinates (x, y) to physical distances relative to the explosion centre using d = 51.4 kpc. Subtract systemic heliocentric velocity (+287 km s^-1) and multiply line-of-sight velocity by time since explosion to get z distance. Divide data cubes into N/S, E/W, Near/Far, and Below/Above (relative to equatorial ring plane) hemispheres to compute fractional emission.
key_parameters: Explosion centre alpha=05:35:27.9875(11), delta=-69:16:11.107(4) (ICRF J2015.0); threshold 1x or 2x noise level
assumptions: Homologous (free) expansion since the explosion; distance = 51.4 kpc; systemic velocity = +287 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Derive observational fractional mass-velocity distributions and summary velocity parameters
recipe.method: Convert 3D spatial distances to 3D radial velocities by dividing radial distance by time since explosion. Bin fractional intensities in increments of 100 or 300 km s^-1. Apply a 3-point moving average and compute v_peak, width (difference between 25th and 75th percentiles), and v_max (95th percentile of molecular mass) with uncertainties via a 1000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation.
key_parameters: 1000 Monte Carlo iterations, 20% standard deviation per data point, 3-point moving average, percentiles: 25th, 75th, 95th
assumptions: Ejecta are optically thin at the observed wavelengths, in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), and at a uniform temperature; constant expansion velocity

recipe.goal: Estimate 3D dust mass-velocity distribution from ALMA Band 7 continuum
recipe.method: Using ALMA Band 7 continuum data (315 GHz), compute dust mass vs velocity under two approximations: (1) all dust velocities are in the plane of the sky; (2) ballistic expansion up to 3500 km s^-1 with dust density declining as r^-2 along the line of sight.
key_parameters: Maximum shell velocity = 3500 km s^-1; radial density profile proportional to r^-2
assumptions: Dust has uniform temperature and negligible optical depth; ballistic expansion; r^-2 density profile

recipe.goal: Compute C+O and Si+O mass-velocity distributions and 3D maps from hydrodynamical explosion simulations
recipe.method: Evolve 15 core-collapse SN models to ~1 yr with PROMETHEUS-HOTB. In each cell, compute maximal C+O mass from min(C, O) stoichiometry, then react remaining O* with Si to form Si+O. Integrate over cell volumes and bin by velocity. For 3D visual comparison, map 3D spherical simulations at t ~ 1 yr onto a 512^3 Cartesian grid, smooth by 8^3 grid cells, interpolate onto a 160^3 grid, and plot every second point in the line-of-sight direction.
key_parameters: Simulation time ~321-373 days (~1 yr); tracer 56X fraction = 0%, 50%, or 100%; Cartesian grid 512^3 smoothed by 8^3 and interpolated to 160^3
assumptions: Carbon binds with oxygen first to form C+O, and only remaining oxygen reacts with silicon to form Si+O; homologous expansion after t ~ 1 yr

recipe.goal: Fit plane to the punctured CO shell and estimate neutron-star kick direction from C+O / CO centre of mass
recipe.method: Fit a 3D plane a(x-x0) + b(y-y0) + c(z-z0) = 0 to the CO data via least-squares minimisation of point-to-plane distances (both fixed to origin and free) and compute angle to the equatorial ring. In simulations, correlate NS kick direction (at t_pb = 2.5 s) with the centre-of-mass direction of C+O above density thresholds F_rho(C+O) = [0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05, 0.01] at t ~ 1 yr. Compute the emission-weighted centre of observed CO to infer the SN 1987A kick vector.
key_parameters: Density thresholds F_rho(C+O) = [0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05, 0.01] (fiducial 15% of maximum density); NS kick evaluated at t_pb = 2.5 s
assumptions: Correlation between the centre of mass of the densest C+O ejecta and the NS kick direction in simulations applies to the observed CO emission in SN 1987A

score_reason: Raw ALMA project codes and simulation archive URL are clearly stated, and the mathematical recipes for 3D mapping, C+O/Si+O stoichiometry, and uncertainty analysis are well documented. However, reduced cubes are only available on request, analysis scripts are not released, some CASA imaging details are deferred to earlier papers or omitted, and 3D model viewing angles were chosen manually.
rediscovery_reason: All four ALMA project codes are public in the ALMA archive, the transformation from spectral line cubes to 3D maps and 1D fractional mass-velocity distributions is straightforward and well-specified, and the summary velocity statistics (v_peak, width, v_max), hemispheric emission ratios, and plane inclination angle provide clear quantitative answer keys.
